definitions.explanation: Something whose outcome cannot be predicted and depends heavily on luck or circumstance, such as a contest, election, or business venture.

examples.japanese: {勝負|しょうぶ}は{水物|みずもの}だ。
examples.english: A contest is a matter of chance.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}は{水物|みずもの}だとよく{言|い}われる。
examples.english: Elections are often said to be unpredictable.

examples.japanese: {商売|しょうばい}は{水物|みずもの}で、{来年|らいねん}どうなるかは{誰|だれ}にも{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: Business is unpredictable; no one knows what next year will bring.

notes:
Almost always used as a predicate (Xは{水物|みずもの}だ) to stress that an outcome is uncertain. Literally "water thing," from the image of something that flows and keeps changing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {勝負|しょうぶ}は{水物|みずもの}: the outcome of a match is unpredictable
- {人気|にんき}は{水物|みずもの}: popularity is fickle

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {運次第|うんしだい}: depending on luck — focuses specifically on luck
- {不確実|ふかくじつ}: uncertain — neutral and more formal
